review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

4:1.sourceText: Οὕτως ἡμᾶς λογιζέσθω ἄνθρωπος ὡς ὑπηρέτας Χριστοῦ καὶ οἰκονόμους μυστηρίων Θεοῦ.
4:1.targetText: So then, men ought to regard us as servants of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God.

4:2.sourceText: ὧδε λοιπὸν ζητεῖται ἐν τοῖς οἰκονόμοις ἵνα πιστός τις εὑρεθῇ.
4:2.targetText: Now it is required of stewards that they be found faithful.

groups.note: λοιπόν ("moreover") is rendered Now.
ἐν ("among") is rendered of after required.
The indefinite τις ("someone") is rendered they.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves ὧδε ("in this case") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:3.sourceText: ἐμοὶ δὲ εἰς ἐλάχιστόν ἐστιν ἵνα ὑφ’ ὑμῶν ἀνακριθῶ ἢ ὑπὸ ἀνθρωπίνης ἡμέρας· ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ ἐμαυτὸν ἀνακρίνω·
4:3.targetText: I care very little, however, if I am judged by you or by any human court. In fact, I do not even judge myself.

groups.note: The dative ἐμοί ("to me") becomes the English subject.
εἰς ἐλάχιστόν ἐστιν ("it is a very small thing") is rendered care very little.
ἡμέρας ("day") is rendered court.

4:4.sourceText: οὐδὲν γὰρ ἐμαυτῷ σύνοιδα, ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἐν τούτῳ δεδικαίωμαι· ὁ δὲ ἀνακρίνων με Κύριός ἐστιν.
4:4.targetText: My conscience is clear, but that does not vindicate me. It is the Lord who judges me.

groups.note: οὐδὲν ἐμαυτῷ σύνοιδα ("I am aware of nothing against myself") is rendered My conscience is clear.
ἐν τούτῳ ("by this") becomes the English subject that.
The passive δεδικαίωμαι ("I am justified") is rendered actively.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves γάρ untranslated.
BSB leaves δέ untranslated.

4:5.sourceText: ὥστε μὴ πρὸ καιροῦ τι κρίνετε, ἕως ἂν ἔλθῃ ὁ Κύριος, ὃς καὶ φωτίσει τὰ κρυπτὰ τοῦ σκότους καὶ φανερώσει τὰς βουλὰς τῶν καρδιῶν· καὶ τότε ὁ ἔπαινος γενήσεται ἑκάστῳ ἀπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ.
4:5.targetText: Therefore judge nothing before the appointed time; wait until the Lord comes. He will bring to light what is hidden in darkness and will expose the motives of men’s hearts. At that time each will receive his praise from God.

groups.note: μὴ … τι ("not … anything") is rendered nothing.
The genitive τοῦ σκότους ("of darkness") is rendered in darkness.
The article is rendered as the possessive his.
γενήσεται ("will come") is rendered will receive, with each as subject.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:6.sourceText: Ταῦτα δέ, ἀδελφοί, μετεσχημάτισα εἰς ἐμαυτὸν καὶ Ἀπολλῶν δι’ ὑμᾶς, ἵνα ἐν ἡμῖν μάθητε τό Μὴ ὑπὲρ ἃ γέγραπται, ἵνα μὴ εἷς ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἑνὸς φυσιοῦσθε κατὰ τοῦ ἑτέρου.
4:6.targetText: Brothers, I have applied these things to myself and Apollos for your benefit, so that you may learn from us not to go beyond what is written. Then you will not take pride in one man over another.

groups.note: δι’ ὑμᾶς ("for your sake") is rendered for your benefit.
ἵνα ("so that") is rendered Then.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.
The article τό introduces the quoted saying; English has no counterpart.

4:7.sourceText: τίς γάρ σε διακρίνει; τί δὲ ἔχεις ὃ οὐκ ἔλαβες; εἰ δὲ καὶ ἔλαβες, τί καυχᾶσαι ὡς μὴ λαβών;
4:7.targetText: For who makes you so superior? What do you have that you did not receive? And if you did receive it, why do you boast as though you did not?

groups.note: διακρίνει ("distinguishes") is rendered makes … so superior.
λαβών ("having received") is represented by did, standing for did receive.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.
BSB leaves καί ("indeed") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for receive.
A participle has no person; English supplies you.

4:8.sourceText: ἤδη κεκορεσμένοι ἐστέ· ἤδη ἐπλουτήσατε· χωρὶς ἡμῶν ἐβασιλεύσατε· καὶ ὄφελόν γε ἐβασιλεύσατε, ἵνα καὶ ἡμεῖς ὑμῖν συνβασιλεύσωμεν.
4:8.targetText: Already you have all you want. Already you have become rich. Without us, you have become kings. How I wish you really were kings, so that we might be kings with you!

groups.note: The perfect participle with ἐστέ ("you have been filled") is rendered you have all you want.
Same word, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

4:9.sourceText: δοκῶ γάρ, ὁ Θεὸς ἡμᾶς τοὺς ἀποστόλους ἐσχάτους ἀπέδειξεν ὡς ἐπιθανατίους, ὅτι θέατρον ἐγενήθημεν τῷ κόσμῳ καὶ ἀγγέλοις καὶ ἀνθρώποις.
4:9.targetText: For it seems to me that God has displayed us apostles at the end of the procession, like prisoners appointed for death. We have become a spectacle to the whole world, to angels as well as to men.

targetPhrases.text: at the end of the procession

groups.note: ἐσχάτους ("last") is rendered at the end of the procession.
ἐπιθανατίους ("condemned to death") is rendered prisoners appointed for death.

4:10.sourceText: ἡμεῖς μωροὶ διὰ Χριστόν, ὑμεῖς δὲ φρόνιμοι ἐν Χριστῷ· ἡμεῖς ἀσθενεῖς, ὑμεῖς δὲ ἰσχυροί· ὑμεῖς ἔνδοξοι, ἡμεῖς δὲ ἄτιμοι.
4:10.targetText: We are fools for Christ, but you are wise in Christ. We are weak, but you are strong. You are honored, but we are dishonored.

4:11.sourceText: ἄχρι τῆς ἄρτι ὥρας καὶ πεινῶμεν καὶ διψῶμεν καὶ γυμνιτεύομεν καὶ κολαφιζόμεθα καὶ ἀστατοῦμεν
4:11.targetText: To this very hour we are hungry and thirsty, we are poorly clothed, we are brutally treated, we are homeless.

groups.note: τῆς ἄρτι ("the present") is rendered this very.

BSB lists these clauses without and.

4:12.sourceText: καὶ κοπιῶμεν ἐργαζόμενοι ταῖς ἰδίαις χερσίν· λοιδορούμενοι εὐλογοῦμεν, διωκόμενοι ἀνεχόμεθα,
4:12.targetText: We work hard with our own hands. When we are vilified, we bless; when we are persecuted, we endure it;

groups.note: κοπιῶμεν ἐργαζόμενοι ("we toil, working") is rendered We work hard.
ἴδιος ("one's own") is rendered our own.
The dative χερσίν is rendered with … hands.

4:13.sourceText: δυσφημούμενοι παρακαλοῦμεν· ὡς περικαθάρματα τοῦ κόσμου ἐγενήθημεν, πάντων περίψημα ἕως ἄρτι.
4:13.targetText: when we are slandered, we answer gently. Up to this moment we have become the scum of the earth, the refuse of the world.

groups.note: κόσμου ("world") is rendered earth.
πάντων ("of all") is rendered of the world.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves ὡς ("like") untranslated.

4:14.sourceText: Οὐκ ἐντρέπων ὑμᾶς γράφω ταῦτα, ἀλλ’ ὡς τέκνα μου ἀγαπητὰ νουθετῶν.
4:14.targetText: I am not writing this to shame you, but to warn you as my beloved children.

groups.note: ὑμᾶς is the shared object of both participles; BSB repeats you after warn.

4:15.sourceText: ἐὰν γὰρ μυρίους παιδαγωγοὺς ἔχητε ἐν Χριστῷ, ἀλλ’ οὐ πολλοὺς πατέρας· ἐν γὰρ Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ διὰ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου ἐγὼ ὑμᾶς ἐγέννησα.
4:15.targetText: Even if you have ten thousand guardians in Christ, you do not have many fathers; for in Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel.

groups.note: The concessive ἐάν is rendered Even if.
The verb is understood again in the second clause.
ἐγέννησα ("I begot") is rendered became … father.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves γάρ untranslated.
BSB leaves ἀλλά ("yet") untranslated.

4:16.sourceText: παρακαλῶ οὖν ὑμᾶς, μιμηταί μου γίνεσθε.
4:16.targetText: Therefore I urge you to imitate me.

groups.note: μιμηταὶ γίνεσθε ("become imitators") is rendered to imitate after urge.

4:17.sourceText: Διὰ τοῦτο αὐτὸ ἔπεμψα ὑμῖν Τιμόθεον, ὅς ἐστίν μου τέκνον ἀγαπητὸν καὶ πιστὸν ἐν Κυρίῳ, ὃς ὑμᾶς ἀναμνήσει τὰς ὁδούς μου τὰς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, καθὼς πανταχοῦ ἐν πάσῃ ἐκκλησίᾳ διδάσκω.
4:17.targetText: That is why I have sent you Timothy, my beloved and faithful child in the Lord. He will remind you of my way of life in Christ Jesus, which is exactly what I teach everywhere in every church.

groups.note: διὰ τοῦτο ("because of this") is rendered That is why.
ὁδούς ("ways") is rendered way of life.
καθώς ("just as") is rendered exactly what.

4:18.sourceText: ὡς μὴ ἐρχομένου δέ μου πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐφυσιώθησάν τινες·
4:18.targetText: Some of you have become arrogant, as if I were not coming to you.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds of you to specify the group.

4:19.sourceText: ἐλεύσομαι δὲ ταχέως πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἐὰν ὁ Κύριος θελήσῃ, καὶ γνώσομαι οὐ τὸν λόγον τῶν πεφυσιωμένων ἀλλὰ τὴν δύναμιν·
4:19.targetText: But I will come to you shortly, if the Lord is willing, and then I will find out not only what these arrogant people are saying, but what power they have.

groups.note: λόγον ("word") is rendered as the verb phrase are saying.
τῶν πεφυσιωμένων ("the puffed-up") is rendered these arrogant people.

4:21.sourceText: τί θέλετε; ἐν ῥάβδῳ ἔλθω πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἢ ἐν ἀγάπῃ πνεύματί τε πραΰτητος;
4:21.targetText: Which do you prefer? Shall I come to you with a rod, or in love and with a gentle spirit?

groups.note: One ἐν governs both love and spirit; BSB renders it in, then with.
πραΰτητος ("of gentleness") is rendered gentle.
